answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by charging a real, unrecoverable cost per identity rather than per account. Each new agent must publish verifiable work to a shared registry, and its first transaction burns a small proof-of-work fee that is never refunded, even if the identity is later abandoned. Before an agent may touch the wharf where high-value jobs clear, it either locks a sable bond or repeats that burn; the second path is punitive, so ten thousand fake peers cost ten thousand burns. Registries then weight votes by age and sunk cost, making a jetty of fresh clones worthless.
